criterion: The moving panel on the home surface sits behind a dark wash that keeps white lettering readable, holding a still poster frame instead of playing where the visitor has asked for reduced motion.
evaluation_rule: The HOME SURFACE is the front door at the root address. A WASH is a dark gradient laid over the moving panel. REDUCED MOTION is the setting a visitor turns on to stop animation. Yes if the panel moves behind a dark wash with white lettering legible over it, and the same surface shows a still frame with the lettering still legible once reduced motion is asked for. No in every other case: a panel with nothing laid over it, lettering hard to read against it, a panel that never plays at all, a panel that still plays once reduced motion is asked for, or a reduced-motion surface that drops the lettering with the film.

criterion: Neighbouring bands down the home surface are told apart by their change of ground alone, with nothing drawn in the seam between them.
evaluation_rule: A BAND is one full-width horizontal region of the home surface, such as the themed shortlists or the row of highlighted places. Yes if nothing is drawn in the seam between two neighbouring bands. No if a rule, a border, a divider line or a drop shadow marks any of those seams.

criterion: A guide document's cover is a generated first page rather than a photograph, carrying a title set in the display serif the product uses for its headings.
evaluation_rule: The GUIDE LIBRARY is the public surface at the guides address listing every downloadable guide document: one for each published place that carries one, plus three REGIONAL guides that belong to no place at all. The DISPLAY SERIF is Playfair Display, the high-contrast face the product sets its headings and place titles in. A REGIONAL guide carries no place name, so its cover carries its own title alone. Yes if every cover reads as a generated page, its title set in that serif over a plain ground. No in every other case: a cover that is a photograph of a place, a cover whose title is set in the narrow sans, or a card standing with no cover at all.

criterion: The desk's sign-in card and its entry list read as the same product as the public guide, drawing only on colours, type families and corner treatments the public surfaces already use.
evaluation_rule: The DESK is the signed-in area at the desk address where staff write the guide. Yes if the sign-in card and the entry list draw on the grounds, text colours, accent, two type families and corner rounding the public surfaces use. No if either introduces a colour, a typeface or a corner treatment that appears nowhere on the public side.

criterion: An editor action is answered by a brief message standing in a corner of the desk over the page the editor acted on, with a fourth action displacing the oldest message.
evaluation_rule: An EDITOR ACTION is a save, a publish or a return to draft. Yes if the message stands in a corner of the desk over the page the editor acted on, the page keeps its scroll position and is not replaced, and a fourth action displaces the oldest message rather than standing beside it. No otherwise: a message centred over the page or one that replaces it, a page that reloads whole or sends the editor to another address, or four messages standing at once.

criterion: A surface that waits keeps the content already drawn, or shows how far an upload has got, rather than filling with a spinner, a disc, a stripe or a shimmer.
evaluation_rule: A SHIMMER is a grey block that pulses where content will arrive. A WAITING SURFACE is one of three: the place index while a filter request is in flight, an upload in the composer, and the gallery while Show more loads. Yes if each of the three holds the content already drawn or shows how far the upload has got. No in every other case: a surface that empties while it waits, one that fills with a spinner, a revolving disc, a striped bar or a pulsing grey block, and any other answer to a wait than holding the drawn content or showing how far the upload has got.

criterion: A month holding zero events is absent from the events calendar rather than drawn as a heading over an empty body.
evaluation_rule: The EVENTS CALENDAR is the public surface listing what is on, grouped under month headings. Yes if the headings run only over months that hold an event, skipping the months between. No if a month heading stands with nothing under it, or if every month of the year is drawn.

criterion: A place entry prints as an article: the chrome gone, the fact panel inline beneath the text, and the picture strip down to its first still, with each link's destination printed after its label.
evaluation_rule: A PLACE ENTRY is the public surface for one place. The FACT PANEL holds the nearest station, the best months and the distance. Yes if a print preview of a place entry drops the header and footer, sets the fact panel under the guide text, shows one still from the strip, and prints each link's destination after its label. No if the print preview carries the chrome, keeps the panel beside the text, prints the whole strip, or prints a link with its destination missing.

criterion: The guide promotion band on the home surface sets a picture on one side against a heading, two sentences and one outlined control on the other, with the row of highlighted places absent altogether where zero places carry the flag.
evaluation_rule: The GUIDE PROMOTION is the band inviting a visitor to download a regional guide. A HIGHLIGHTED place is one staff have flagged for the front page. Yes if, on a wide screen, the promotion is two columns with the picture on one side and a heading, two sentences and one outlined control on the other, and the highlighted row either shows places or is not drawn. No if the promotion is one column on a wide screen, if any of those three elements is missing from its side, or if an empty highlighted band is drawn.

criterion: A single warm orange marks everything a visitor can act on across the public surfaces, and each of the product's four other hues stays in its named role: the secondary amber on the home eyebrow and badge fills, blue on links inside prose, red on a validation failure in a desk form, and teal on the desk's live badge and its publish confirmation.
evaluation_rule: The DESK is the signed-in area at the desk address where staff write the guide; its LIVE BADGE marks an entry the public can see and its PUBLISH CONFIRMATION is the message raised when one goes live. A visitor CAN ACT ON a link, a button, a filter control or a currently selected item. INERT means text, a border or a panel a visitor cannot use. An EYEBROW is the short capitalised label set above a heading. Yes if the orange appears on actionable and selected things alone, and each of the other four hues appears only in the role named here. No if the orange wears on something inert, or if any of those four hues turns up outside its named role.

criterion: Across the guide's public surfaces the running text, its secondary passages and its metadata lines sit at three distinct depths of neutral, with a heading on a light ground darker than all three.
evaluation_rule: RUNNING TEXT is the body prose of a surface. A SECONDARY PASSAGE is a standfirst or an editorial introduction. A METADATA LINE is the small line carrying a count, a date or a caption. Yes if those three read as three distinct depths of neutral and a heading on a light ground reads darker than any of them. No if two of the four read as one colour, or if a metadata line reads darker than the prose it sits under.

criterion: A public surface carries the pale placeholder grey on text a visitor has to read.
evaluation_rule: PLACEHOLDER GREY is the pale grey reserved for the hint text inside an empty field and for a control a visitor cannot use. Yes if that pale grey carries running prose, a place name, a date or any other content a visitor must read on a public surface. No if it stays on hints and unavailable controls alone.

criterion: Movement across the product is one eased character: entrances glide to a stop, exits leave quickly, and the single long reveal on the home surface waits a beat before travelling, with a visitor who has asked for reduced motion getting each of those as a plain change of state.
evaluation_rule: GLIDING TO A STOP means the movement decelerates rather than stopping abruptly. A LONG REVEAL is an entrance that pauses before it moves. REDUCED MOTION is the setting a visitor turns on to stop animation. Yes if every movement decelerates on arrival and accelerates on exit, one entrance on the home surface waits before travelling, and under reduced motion every entrance, exit and position change lands at once with no travel. No in every other case: movements that snap into place, movements that run at a constant rate, a product whose entrances are all eased but none of which waits before travelling, and anything that still travels once reduced motion is asked for.

criterion: Each state badge on the desk entry list carries its own word beside its fill, so the live rows stay tellable from the draft rows in a grey print.
evaluation_rule: The DESK is the signed-in area at the desk address where staff write the guide, and its ENTRY LIST is the table of entries there. A STATE BADGE marks whether an entry is public or unfinished. A GREY PRINT is the same page with all colour removed. Yes if each badge shows a word such as Live or Draft as well as a coloured fill, so the two states stay distinguishable with the colour gone. No if the state is carried by the fill alone, or if the two words are the same.

criterion: At a phone-width window every row of cards on the public surfaces is one column wide: the themed shortlists, the row of highlighted places, the place grid, the guide library and the gallery masonry alike.
evaluation_rule: PHONE WIDTH is a window narrow enough that the navigation has collapsed into its drawer. Yes if all five of those card rows show exactly one card per row at that width. No if any of the five keeps two or more cards side by side at that width.
